summary: Your cover letter clearly states your academic background and highlights relevant hands-on experience managing a social media account. To make your application more competitive, you should directly address the specific technical requirements and tools mentioned in the job description.
strengths: You highlight practical social media management experience through your role with the university debate club.
You connect your academic studies in Business Administration and consumer behavior directly to your interest in marketing.

gaps.why: The job post requires tracking campaign results, but your letter does not mention any experience with analytics tools or measuring social media performance.
gaps.jobPostEvidence: track campaign results in Google Analytics

gaps.why: While you mention posting updates, you do not explain how you plan or schedule this content, which is a key responsibility for the intern role.
The employer lists SEO knowledge as a requirement and email marketing tools as a plus, but your letter does not address either of these areas.
gaps.jobPostEvidence: Basic SEO knowledge and strong written English are required. Experience with email marketing tools is a plus.
